title: Interactive Pathway Cards and Rollback Explorer for Tenant Connectivity
creator: Avery Chen
description: Design an interactive, scan-first surface in the Private Console that helps operators quickly understand tenant cluster connectivity and perform safe rollback actions for recent upgrade rollouts. The core idea is a compact set of 'Pathway Cards' that summarize connectivity, recent latency/egress trends, and a contextual rollback explorer that shows what will change if a rollback is initiated.
background: Private clusters have complex inter-region networking and upgrade workflows. Operators told us they want a single-pane way to: (1) see which tenant requests flow through which hop, (2) understand cost/latency exposure per path, and (3) trigger safe rollbacks with clear impact previews. Existing designs are scattershot across the cluster and rollout pages.
goals: (1) Reduce mean time to awareness for path-level failures; (2) Surface cost/latency trade-offs inline with connectivity; (3) Provide a friction-minimized rollback flow that shows simulated outcomes before commit.
proposed_screens:
1) Tenant Pathway List: compact cards per logical path (eg. tenant-gateway -> edge-proxy -> cluster-nodes -> external-egress). Each card shows status chip, 1-hr latency sparkline, 24h egress cost estimate, and an Expand action.
2) Expanded Card Modal: shows step-by-step hop visualizer with packet-loss %, median latency, last successful health check, and overlay toggles (Latency / Cost / Bandwidth).
3) Rollback Explorer: timeline scrubber of recent rollouts for the selected path, delta preview of routing and capacity changes, flagged dependent tenants, and a one-click safe-rollback with preflight checklist.
4) Simulation Mode: 'What-if' toggle that runs a dry-run against the routing policy engine and displays potential failover routes and cost delta.
mockups: Figma frames include compact list, expanded details modal, rollback timeline, and simulation overlay. See frames: Pathway_List_v3, Pathway_Expanded_v2, Rollback_Explorer_v1.
acceptance_criteria: Pathway List renders correctly for tenants with 1-10 routing hops
Expanded Card shows hop-level metrics and health check history
Rollback Explorer simulates the chosen rollback and surfaces at-risk tenants
Design tokens and spacing align with console style guide
Edge cases: offline clusters and missing metrics show graceful placeholders and clear next steps
recent_comments: 2025-02-14 - PM Morgan Patel: Suggest adding an explicit 'impact surface' line for cost-sensitive tenants.
2025-02-16 - Eng Samir Gupta: Backend needs an aggregated path-cost API; created ENG-1842 to track telemetry contract.
2025-02-20 - Design critique (Cross-team): Consider moving the simulation mode to a secondary action to reduce accidental use — Riley to prototype confirmation flow.
review_feedback: Security review: ensure rollback dry-run does not leak internal topology to non-admin roles. Ops requested an 'undo' snackbar after rollback with a 5-minute reversal window. Accessibility: keyboard focus order for expanded cards must be tested.
decisions: 1) Use card-first approach (list -> expand modal) instead of inline expansion to keep the list scannable. 2) Simulation Mode will be bounded to role=operator and requires audit-log entry. 3) Cost overlay will show estimated 24h delta, not real-time billing data (privacy and API limits).
risks: Overloading the card UI with too many metrics could reduce scanability. Telemetry APIs may not provide consistent per-hop egress breakdown for all clusters — fallback will show aggregated regional costs. Rollback automation must be conservative; push confirmation and dependency warnings.
engineering_notes: Backend contract: GET /internal/paths?tenant_id=... -> returns ordered hops, health, latency_samples, cost_estimate_24h. ENG-1842 tracks batching and caching for these calls. Rollback flow requires POST /rollouts/rollback-preview and POST /rollouts/rollback (with dry_run flag). Engineers have requested simulated payload examples in the spec folder.
next_steps: 1) Iterate prototype to address feedback about simulation placement (due 2025-02-25). 2) Hand off annotated Figma frames and redlines to ENG. 3) Schedule cross-team review with SRE to validate failure-mode messaging. 4) Prepare A/B test plan for rollout visibility and rollback usage metrics.
qa_notes: QA should validate: card list pagination, expanded modal accessibility, rollback preview accuracy for both single-tenant and shared-tenant rollouts, audit log entries on simulation and real rollbacks.
